title: feat(pm): declared unlocked mode where the verify lock has no flock
body:
Fixes #10611

The shared verification lock is now declared **Linux-only**. A host with no usable
`flock` no longer refuses at exit 99 — it runs the command in a **declared unlocked
mode**, writes the degradation into the `VERDICT` line, and prints the disclosure its
PR body must carry.

## The ruling this implements

Maintainer ruling recorded 2026-08-22 (「接受所有」 batch, comment `5377362474`),
verbatim:

> **Ruled:** Option B (the card body's option 4) — the shared verification lock is
> declared **Linux-only**. macOS gets an explicit, **declared unlocked mode** instead of
> a refusal: the degradation is written into the VERDICT line so it is visible and
> auditable, and the disclosure format the two unlocked-verification precedents (#10219,
> #10221) used becomes the official format, plus the one-line documentation change.
> Attached reversal clause: this ruling is to be revisited if macOS becomes a required
> agent host for the fleet — at that point the perl `flock(2)` shim direction (card
> option 3) is the standing preference.

Card options 1 (`brew` prerequisite), 2 (`mkdir` lockfile) and 3 (perl `flock(2)` shim)
are ruled against and are **not** built here. Option 3 exists only inside the reversal
clause, which fires on a maintainer decision.

## Premise re-check, against today's `main`

The card is dated 2026-08-21 and describes PR #10609's state. Re-read at `daacc107`: the
refusal path is still shaped as described — the functional `flock` probe in `preflight`
adds its finding to `PREFLIGHT_PROBLEMS`, and `mode_run` turns any non-empty
`PREFLIGHT_PROBLEMS` into `VERDICT lock-unusable (exit 99) · never acquired · refused
before waiting`. The card's premise holds.

## What changed

**`preflight` splits one finding out of the refusal set.** `PREFLIGHT_PROBLEMS` keeps its
meaning — every entry is a refusal — and the flock finding moves to its own
`PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK` / `PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK_NOTE` pair. Summing the two into one verdict is
precisely what would hide that they lead to opposite outcomes.

**`mode_run` gains one branch,** placed on purpose: *after* the filter preflight (a
command that would measure nothing is refused whether or not there is a lock to spend on
it — the two checks are independent and both still apply) and *before* the budget, the
queue and the fd, none of which mean anything without the primitive.

**`run_unlocked` runs the command with no lock,** prints a `VERDICT command-exit N ·
UNLOCKED (declared) · … the shared verify lock was NEVER taken and NOTHING was serialized
· ran Ns`, and passes the command's own exit code through.

**`--status` reports the degraded host as degraded** rather than as unusable, and stops
answering `lock is free` — a line it can only produce by failing to take a lock it has no
primitive for.

**One documentation line**, in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/true-green.md`, the
per-repo how-to-run index whose own discipline is one line per fact.

## The three things most likely to go wrong, and what pins each

### 1. The `kill -9`-releases invariant

The unlocked path creates **nothing**: no lock file, no holder record, no queue ticket, no
fd 9. There is nothing to reap, so a killed process leaves the host exactly as it found
it, and no sibling can read stale state and conclude the lock is held. That is the
property the rejected `mkdir` option would have given up, so it is pinned rather than
asserted — four self-test cases, three after an ordinary exit and one after a real
`kill -9` mid-run:

```
✓ an unlocked run leaves no lock file
✓ no holder record
✓ no queue ticket directory
✓ and a kill -9 mid-run leaves nothing behind to reap either
```

### 2. Branch on the primitive, never on the platform

The trigger is the **functional** `flock` probe failing — `uname` is never consulted, so a
Linux container without util-linux degrades the same way and a macOS host with brew's
`flock` takes the ordinary locked path.

The probe grew one refinement that is the whole guard against the worst regression here.
The probe file's **creation** is now checked apart from the lock taken on it. A probe file
that cannot be created says nothing whatever about `flock` — the temp dir is unusable,
which is also where the lock file lives — and stays a refusal. Merged into one finding, a
full or read-only `/tmp` on an ordinary Linux host would have read as "no flock" and
silently dropped serialization for every agent in the container. Both halves are pinned:

```
✓ a host problem that is NOT the flock one still exits 99
✓ and says lock-unusable, not queue-timeout
✓ and does not run the command
✓ and does NOT degrade to unlocked — flock was never the thing that failed
✓ a host WITH a working flock never enters unlocked mode
```

### 3. The locked path is unaffected — measured, not asserted

Both scripts were driven through the same seven-part locked-path suite on this host (which
has `flock from util-linux 2.39.3`): uncontended acquisition, exit-code passthrough,
contention with a real holder and a waiter that times out, `--status` with a live holder,
`--status` once free, `--show-budget` default and clamped, and a usage error. Transcripts
normalized only for pids/durations/paths (`s/[0-9][0-9]*/N/g`) and diffed:

- `git show origin/main:scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` → **before**
- this branch's `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` → **after**

`diff` reports **exactly one hunk**: the four lines added to the `--help`/usage text
describing the new mode. Every `ACQUIRED`, `VERDICT command-exit`, `VERDICT
queue-timeout`, `state:`, `queue:` and `budget:` line is byte-for-byte identical:

```
### N contention: holder + waiter that times out
os-verify-lock: VERDICT queue-timeout (exit N) · never acquired · waited Ns · holder pid N, held Ns — sleep N
```

The full `--self-test` is the second half of that evidence: it drives the real acquisition
path under contention (FIFO ordering of three staggered waiters, legacy free-hand `flock`
coexistence in both directions, the frozen-clock backstop, the ordinary full-budget
timeout) and passes 88/88 at this branch's head.

## Reverse verification

Both legs mutate the committed file under a `trap '<restore>' EXIT INT TERM`, confirm the
mutation landed on disk by grep-counting the removed text **and** the injected marker
before running anything, and restore to a byte-identical tree (`diff -q` against a
pristine copy). **No rebuild leg applies:** the subject is a shell script executed directly
by `bash`, with no `dist/` between the edit and the run, so the mutation reaches the
measured code by editing the file and nothing else — stated because a missing rebuild is
the usual way an ablation reads green while measuring the wrong tree.

| leg | mutation (confirmed on disk) | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| revert the ruling | `PREFLIGHT_NO_FLOCK=1` → `pf_add "ABLATION-refuse-on-no-flock"` (marker count 1→0 / 0→1) | **8 cases red**, incl. `an unusable flock RUNS the command unlocked instead of refusing` and `--status calls a no-flock host unlocked rather than unusable` |
| merge the probe checks back | the `: > "$probe"` creation guard deleted, marker `ABLATION-merged-probe` injected (1→0 / 0→1) | **5 cases red**, incl. `a host problem that is NOT the flock one still exits 99` and `and does NOT degrade to unlocked` |

The direction is plain "goes red" on both legs, which is what was predicted before running
them.

## The exit-99 refusal has no other callers

Grepped for every reference to this wrapper in the repo. The only consumers are
`.github/workflows/lint.yml` (which runs `--self-test`, updated here),
`scripts/check-pnpm-filter-targets.mjs` and `scripts/pnpm-filter-targets.mjs` (which name
the file as a rule-owning path, not its exit codes), and two prose docs. **Nothing branches
on exit 99 from a missing `flock`.** The code is not repurposed either: an unlocked run
passes the command's own exit code through, so 99 keeps meaning "never got a turn" and
never doubles as "this host has no lock" — the `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` statement `99 仍
专指「没排到」` stays accurate as written, which is why the one doc line went elsewhere.

Note also that `AGENTS.md` (961/961) and `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` (405/405) sit at zero
headroom under `check:pm-skill-ratchet`, whose ceilings may only be raised with a
maintainer ruling quoted in the raising PR. `references/true-green.md` carries no ceiling
(verified against the `CEILINGS` map, not recalled), which is where the one line landed.

## Verification

Everything below ran at `ec001e60`, the final commit, on Linux with a working `flock`.

- `bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh --self-test` → exit 0 · `✓ os-verify-lock self-test:
  all cases pass.` (88 cases; 21 of them new or rewritten)
- Gate union re-derived at the final commit with
  `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths passed —
  the script derives the change set from the merge base itself). It named 11 families;
  all 11 ran green, plus 5 more this diff visibly touches. Exit codes captured before any
  pipe; each line below is the gate's **own** printed verdict, not a bare `$?`:

| gate | exit | its own verdict line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check:cross-package-test-inputs` | 0 | `OK: 14 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared, and turbo.json hashes every declared glob.` |
| `check:doc-authoring` | 0 | `✓ doc authoring guard: 389 files clean — no bare metadata literals.` |
| `check:doc-formula-expressions` | 0 | `✓ …: 22 record-scoped formula example(s) across 420 files / 1449 TS blocks judged clean` |
| `check:entry-guard` | 0 | `✓ check:entry-guard: 139 scripts/ file(s) — every entry guard goes through invoked-as.mjs` |
| `check:parse-guard` | 0 | `✓ check:parse-guard: 138 scripts/ file(s) — every TypeScript parse goes through ts-parse.mjs.` |
| `check:pm-governed-merges` | 0 | `✓ check-governed-merges --self-test: 129 assertions …` |
| `check:pm-skill-id-lint` | 0 | `✓ check-skill-id-lint: 21 file(s) clean (pattern /#[0-9]{3,}/g).` |
| `check:pnpm-filter-targets` | 0 | `✓ check:pnpm-filter-targets: 120/148 --filter occurrence(s) across 25 file(s) resolve …` |
| `check:skill-frame-sync` | 0 | `✓ check-skill-frame-sync: 4 copies of the decision frame are structurally isomorphic across 3 files` |
| `check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` | 0 | `OK: all 89 declared cross-package glob(s) (77 unique) are covered …` |
| `check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` | 0 | same script as the first row, run standalone |
| `check:nul-bytes` | 0 | `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 6459 text file(s) -- 6459 tracked, 0 untracked-not-ignored; skipped 5 binary; no raw ASCII control bytes).` |
| `check:pm-skill-ratchet` | 0 | `✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: CLAUDE.md is 86 lines (ceiling 86; headroom 0).` |
| `check:pm-dispatch-gates` | 0 | `✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 557 cases pass.` |
| `check:pm-label-desc-cap` | 0 | `✓ check:pm-label-desc-cap: 21 label descriptions … all ≤100 characters` |
| `check:where-matcher` | 0 | `✓ where-matcher conformance holds: 290 matcher(s) discovered …` |

The last five are not in the derived list. Four are the families `--residue` flags as
`silent`-because-artifact-roster with the roster sitting in a directory one of these paths
is in — a verdict that "reads as a clearance and is not" — so they were run rather than
inferred; `check:nul-bytes` is run on any edit.

**Declared narrowing — repo-wide `pnpm lint` was not run, and this is a measurement rather
than a skip.** Three pieces of evidence, all read from the tooling rather than assumed:

1. **Population, from eslint's own config.** Every `files:` glob in `eslint.config.mjs`
   names extensions `cjs cts js jsx mjs mts ts tsx`. Neither `sh` nor `md` appears.
2. **Count, from `--format json`.** `npx eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over both
   changed paths → exit 0, **2 result objects, 0 errors**, each carrying the single message
   `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied.`
3. **Invariance for untouched files.** Type-aware linting is off by construction — the
   config's own comment at line 328 reads `(no parserOptions.project, no typed
   @typescript-eslint rules)` — so no untouched file's judgment can move because of a diff
   that adds no TypeScript.

`pnpm lint` therefore has zero files to say anything about here. CI runs the farm anyway.

**No changeset**, and the `skip-changeset` label is applied: the diff is a repo-internal
`scripts/pm/` shell script plus an internal `.claude/` doc, so nothing is published and no
package version moves. Line delta on the internal skills surface: `true-green.md` 32 → 34
(+2); the published `skills/` catalog is untouched.

## Scope

No other card is addressed here. #10303 remains open and stays `pm:blocked` on this one
until it lands; it was not touched. The reversal clause's perl `flock(2)` shim is not
built.
